name: MCP List Servers
description: List the MCP servers configured on this platform.

function.name: mcp_list_servers
function.description: List the external MCP servers configured and enabled on this platform (e.g. 'claude-code'), with their transport (stdio or http). Cheap: it only reads configuration and does not connect to any server. Use it to find out which MCP servers are available, then call mcp_list_tools(server) to see a server's tools and mcp_call to use them. Requires the MCP Client plugin to be enabled.

mock_response: {"servers":[{"name":"claude-code","transport":"stdio"}],"hint":"Call mcp_list_tools(server) to see a server's tools, then mcp_call to use one."}

name: MCP List Tools
description: List tools available on configured MCP servers.

function.name: mcp_list_tools
function.description: List the tools exposed by external MCP servers configured on this platform (e.g. 'claude-code'). By default this returns a compact listing: each tool's name, a short description and an argument signature such as 'presentation_id:string!, title:string?' ('!' = required, '?' = optional, 'mode[a|b]' = allowed values). The raw JSON input schema of every tool would be tens of thousands of characters and gets truncated by the runtime, so schemas are only included on request: pass filter='<substring of the tool name>' to get the matching tools together with their full input_schema, or include_schema=true for every tool (large toolsets have schemas omitted automatically). Use names_only=true when you only need the tool names. Call mcp_list_servers first to see which servers are configured, then call this before mcp_call to discover valid tool names and their expected arguments. Requires the MCP Client plugin to be enabled.

server.description: Name of a configured MCP server (e.g. 'claude-code'). Omit to list tools from all configured servers.

names_only.description: Return only the tool names, without descriptions or schemas. Cheapest way to see which tools exist.

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring (a regex is also accepted) matched against tool name and description. Returns only matching tools, together with their full input_schema. Preferred over include_schema when you need exact arguments for a few tools.

include_schema.description: Include every tool's full JSON input_schema. Only useful for a small toolset; oversized listings have their schemas omitted automatically.

mock_response: {"server":"claude-code","tool_count":2,"shown":2,"tools":[{"name":"Bash","description":"Run a shell command","args":"command:string!"},{"name":"Read","description":"Read a file from disk","args":"file_path:string!, offset:integer?"}],"hint":"Call mcp_list_tools(server, filter='<substring>') for full input_schema."}

name: MCP Call
description: Call a tool on a configured MCP server.

function.name: mcp_call
function.description: Invoke a tool on an external MCP server configured on this platform (e.g. run Claude Code's Bash tool via the 'claude-code' server). Call mcp_list_servers to see configured server names and mcp_list_tools to discover tool names and each tool's input schema, then pass the tool's arguments as a JSON object. Requires the MCP Client plugin to be enabled.

server.description: Name of a configured MCP server (e.g. 'claude-code'). Discover valid names via mcp_list_tools.

tool.description: Name of the tool to invoke on the server (e.g. 'Bash'), exactly as returned by mcp_list_tools.

arguments.description: Arguments for the tool as a JSON object, matching the tool's input_schema from mcp_list_tools.

timeout_sec.description: Optional timeout in seconds for this call. Capped at the admin-configured maximum.
